bull.b: Aggressive, repeatable unit growth under a franchise model drives recurring royalty and fee revenue while minimizing capital intensity. A large pipeline and stated push toward a >10,000-unit global footprint provide durable revenue leverage and long-term scale benefits for margins and brand penetration.

Sustained, high restaurant-level margins reflect durable unit economics and pricing power for a limited-menu, delivery-friendly concept. Healthy operating and EBITDA margins support franchised royalty streams and give the company structural capacity to fund expansion, marketing, and shareholder returns.

Consistent operating cash flow and meaningful free cash flow allow management to reinvest in unit growth, execute opportunistic M&A and return capital to shareholders via buybacks and dividends. Strong cash generation is a durable pillar for financing expansion without heavy equity issuance.

bear.b: Persistently negative equity raises financial fragility, complicates leverage assessment and reduces cushioning against downturns. Even with recent debt reduction, a compromised capital structure limits flexibility for sustained investments or shocks and raises refinancing and stakeholder risk over the medium term.

bear.t: Same-Store Sales Pressure in Core Markets
bear.b: Material comp declines and concentration in lower-income urban trade areas create a structural headwind to royalty-linked revenue and cash flow. If frequency and visit patterns remain impaired, recurring franchise income and unit-level economics may face prolonged weakness despite new openings.

bear.t: Volatile Free Cash Flow & Profit Normalization
bear.b: While FCF is meaningful in aggregate, recent sharp volatility and sub‑100% cash conversion increase the risk that cash available for growth and returns will fluctuate. Coupled with negative equity, uneven FCF raises the chance that capital allocation must be reprioritized during stress periods.
